system_overview: This specification refines the EWD998Chan termination detection algorithm by replacing natural number node identifiers with arbitrary identifiers (such as strings) organized into a ring. It also generalizes the initiator to be any chosen node rather than always node 0, adds vector clocks for distributed event ordering, and tracks the number of token passes after termination for worst-case complexity analysis. The specification demonstrates how to model vector clocks in TLA+ and how to decouple the algorithm from a specific node numbering scheme.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a finite set of nodes organized into a ring using a bijective ring function. One node is chosen as the initiator of token rounds. Each node has an inbox for receiving messages, a local vector clock, and the standard termination detection state (activation, color, counter). Payload messages carry a source identifier and a vector clock timestamp.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) activation status of each node, (2) color of each node, (3) a counter for each node, (4) an inbox for each node containing typed messages (token and payload messages with vector clock timestamps), (5) a vector clock for each node mapping all nodes to clock values, and (6) a pass counter tracking the number of token passes since termination.
initial_state: All counters are zero. The initiator's vector clock starts with its own entry at 1, all other entries at zero; other nodes' clocks are all zeros. The token starts at a specific node position (chosen for worst-case analysis). All nodes start inactive with black color. The pass counter is initialized based on whether the system starts in a terminated state.
actions: The algorithm defines the following parameterized actions (parameterized by node identity): (1) Initiate probe: the initiator consumes a token from its inbox, merges vector clocks, and sends a fresh white token to its ring successor. (2) Pass token: a non-initiator inactive node consumes a token, merges vector clocks, and passes an updated token to its ring successor. Both token actions increment the pass counter. (3) Send message: an active node increments its counter and clock, then sends a payload message with its updated clock to another node. (4) Receive message: a node consumes a payload message, merges vector clocks, decrements its counter, paints itself black, and becomes active. (5) Deactivate: an active node becomes inactive, increments its clock, and resets the pass counter if the system just terminated.
safety_properties: The specification refines EWD998Chan (with a refinement mapping that translates identifiers back to natural numbers), inheriting all its safety properties. Additionally, a worst-case bound property states that termination is detected within at most three full token rounds after the system terminates.
liveness_properties: Inherited from the EWD998Chan specification through refinement.
model_bounds: A state constraint is inherited from EWD998Chan, limiting payload message counts and counters.
additional_assumptions: The node set is finite and non-empty. Nodes are organized into a simple cycle (ring). The initiator is deterministically chosen. The specification uses a ring successor function and provides operators for converting between node identifiers and natural numbers for the refinement mapping. Weak fairness is assumed for each node's system actions.
